chapters.title: Chapter 47: Lin Fang The Man of Culture
paragraphs: Leon knew he couldn’t waste time contemplating this tragedy any longer. He had the causality now—finally. That meant he could purchase the book that might hold the information he desperately needed.
#. Self-Biography of the Great Master Longstaff _(Rare – Book)_

An autobiographical disaster penned by a self-proclaimed genius who claims to have seduced a dragon, outdueled a sword saint, and dated a fairy. Contains way too many shirtless illustrations and footnotes about "techniques" that definitely aren’t martial. _My journey from Lowest of the Low Ascendant Realm to Divine Realm._
Price:100 casualties
Vendor: _Master Longstaff the Endlessly Accomplished_
It was suspiciously cheap, which made it easier for Leon to gamble on. Still, from the description alone, he already knew it would contain... questionable content.
In his previous world, he’d died at the tender age of sixteen. Young. Far too young.
He hadn’t even finished high school. Hadn’t traveled. Hadn’t really lived. But somehow, against all odds, he had managed to have a girlfriend—briefly.
One week.

Seven days of awkward hand-holding, clammy palms, and bashful smiles traded between classes. It was clumsy and innocent, the kind of relationship that barely qualified as real by adult standards—but to him, back then, it had meant everything.
And then Devon happened.
His obnoxious, loud, effortlessly magnetic stepbrother who couldn’t, for the life of him, mind his own damn business.
A single joke. A badly timed comment. One smile too many in the wrong direction. That was all it took to shatter the fragile thing Leon had barely begun to build.
She left him the very next day—convinced he was using her to mask a secret crush on Devon. Not angry. Just... confused. Hurt.
He’d tried to explain. Told her it was all a misunderstanding. But nothing worked.

Leon still remembered standing in the school courtyard, the late afternoon sun casting long shadows over the pavement, his backpack slung carelessly over one shoulder. He’d watched her walk away without a word. Tears in her eyes. No explanation. No confrontation. Just silence that screamed louder than any goodbye.
The ache he’d felt then hadn’t vanished. It had only buried itself deeper.
It had been the first time he’d genuinely wanted to kill Devon—his infuriating, smug, impossibly obnoxious gay stepbrother.
Thinking about the past still made his jaw tighten, but he’d moved on.
’That girl wasn’t right for me. If she left just because of some weird misunderstanding and the delusions she had in her head, then it was never going to last.’
Leon shoved those dead old feelings aside and focused. He thought about buying the book. Instantly, a translucent golden message appeared in front of him on the shimmering interface.
[Are you sure you want to use 100 Causality to buy _Self-Biography of the Great Master Longstaff_ _(Rare – Book)_?]
’Yes.’
He answered in his mind.
The moment his intent was confirmed, the balance in the upper corner of the interface changed.
[Causality: 288,900]
A thick book glitched into existence before him, much like the golden treasure chest had disappeared—reality bending, then snapping back.
Leon caught the hefty tome before it could hit the ground.

Just from the cover—featuring a naked woman with cat ears—he already understood the kind of journey he was in for. The title and author’s name, _Master Longstaff the Endlessly Accomplished_, had been a red flag, but the art? The art removed all doubt.
He stared at the cover for a moment longer. It was his first time seeing a true catwoman. Curiosity warred with secondhand embarrassment.

Shaking his head, Leon walked to the carved mahogany study table, pulled out a plush cushioned chair, and took a comfortable seat. But the moment his eyes drifted back to the sheer _thickness_ of the book, something clicked in his mind.
’Why didn’t I think of it earlier?’
He could materialize things inside his Time Dimension—if they were already stored in his soul-bound inventory. Which meant... he could read this inside. It wouldn’t cost him any time at all.
With a thought, he stored the book and immediately activated the Dimensional Hourglass. Or rather, its ability—he no longer needed the artifact itself.
The world shimmered around him. In an instant, he was inside.
The Time Dimension appeared once more—vast, silent, endless. Smooth stone ground stretched into a pale horizon, the air saturated with a sense of stillness.

The book materialized in his hand the moment he thought of it. He took a seat on the warm, flat floor and opened it with cautious fingers. It had been a long time since he’d read anything for pleasure.
Within minutes, his face turned red.
He blushed. More than once. There were moments when his brows rose in shock, his eyes widened, his mouth even hung open.
The contents were... graphic. Brazen. Utterly shameless.
But also fascinating.
After six continuous hours of reading, Leon finally closed the book and let out a long breath.
There was a hint of respect in his expression.
Not because Lin Fang had reached the Lesser Divinity rank—practically an immortal with limitless lifespan. That wasn’t what impressed Leon.
It was the _way_ he had done it.

In the story, Lin Fang wasn’t the most talented. Others were born with higher affinities, better backgrounds, stronger destinies. He never even tried to outpace them. He simply carved out a strange, unexpected path—and stuck to it.
Lin Fang had been born in the Ascendant Realm on a planet called Blue Star. His journey began when his fiancée broke off their engagement. He had failed to awaken an affinity—even at age eighteen.
After being kicked out of his house, Lin Fang nearly died saving a voluptuous woman from thugs. He expected gratitude. Instead, she fled, leaving him to fight alone.

But in that moment, something triggered. He awakened a Rank 5 Illusion Affinity. Not as impressive as the geniuses with Rank 6 and multiple affinities—but rare enough. If used well, it could still make him strong. Strong enough to teach a few lessons. Especially to his former fiancée.

Lin Fang wasn’t handsome, but he was decently above average. Since childhood, he had dreamed of building his own harem. Not one filled with impossibly beautiful genius women—those were too much trouble—but with warm, loyal, quietly attractive girls who wouldn’t drag him into chaos.
During his Class Awakening Trial, he received a Unique S-ranked class: _Illusionary Playboy._
And that was the start of it.
He joined a sect to gain strength, made it into the inner circle, and there met the voluptuous library mistress—his first real teacher and his first true love.
She taught him everything.
Not about cultivation.
About sex.
Big breasts. A round ass as soft as sponge. She didn’t go easy on him.
Leon didn’t even try to hide his expression at this point. The scenes were vivid. The writing... a little too descriptive.

According to the book, Lin Fang hadn’t used tricks. Well—maybe a few. His class had its perks. But in the end, the library mistress spared him because, as she said, he had the biggest cock she had ever seen.
And so began Lin Fang’s unconventional journey. He stayed far from prodigies and entanglements, built a harem of curvy, cheerful women, and focused on safety, comfort, and longevity.
They weren’t the most talented girls. But they had soft personalities, big hearts, and—as the book kept emphasizing—amazing boobs and asses.
That, apparently, had been enough for Lin Fang.

chapters.title: Chapter 48: Lin Fang The Man of Culture (2)
paragraphs: The sex scenes described in Lin Fang’s autobiography weren’t merely detailed—they were exhaustively vivid, confidently narrated, and meticulously instructional. Each page brimmed with explicit pointers on various techniques to please a woman: emotional connection, pacing, rhythmic thrusts, intimate touches, and even spiritual synchronization during the climax.

Leon had never encountered literature like this. Initially, he felt embarrassed, but soon he realized those weren’t empty boasts—they sprang from genuine experience. He committed each technique to memory, knowing they represented valuable, perhaps even indispensable, knowledge that would benefit him someday.

But Lin Fang’s seemingly unstoppable luck eventually crashed spectacularly. Misfortune struck when he set his eyes on a particularly captivating elf woman in a tavern near the Divine Realm’s Adventurers’ Guild. Using illusions to enhance his already decent appearance, subtle charm spells, and unique class abilities that were intentionally only hinted at in the book, Lin Fang confidently approached his target. His fourteen beautiful harem members observed from a nearby table, not only unbothered by his efforts but actively supportive, eager to welcome another companion.

Unfortunately, his target wasn’t just any ordinary elf—she was secretly the heir to an influential and powerful elven clan, traveling incognito. She effortlessly pierced through his deceptive charms and illusions, identifying him immediately.

Lin Fang didn’t even manage to hold her hand or exchange flirtatious banter. Yet, that brief encounter ignited her fury, resulting in Lin Fang’s name being added overnight to bounty lists circulated across every major realm. Wanted posters with his likeness appeared rapidly, spreading throughout taverns, guild halls, and city gates.

He narrowly escaped the tavern alive, forced to activate one of his precious one-time use legendary-ranked escape treasures, disappearing alongside his fourteen loyal women amidst a flash of blinding magic.
Lin Fang lost nearly everything—his accumulated wealth, his status, his dignity—but fortunately, his precious companions remained safe and intact.

Since that fateful day, Lin Fang had retreated from the public eye entirely. His exact whereabouts became uncertain, shrouded in mystery. Rumors whispered he now hid somewhere within the vast expanse of the Ascendant Realm, or possibly in some obscure corner of the Ethereal or even Divine Realms.
His concluding paragraphs in the autobiography didn’t carry regret or bitterness. Instead, they resonated like a joyful toast to a life thoroughly enjoyed. He proudly proclaimed:

"No regrets. I’m living my best life hidden in paradise with fourteen incredible women. I’ve reached Lesser Divinity, achieved the pinnacle of what I desire, and woke up every morning surrounded by softness and warmth. If this isn’t a success, I don’t know what is."

Leon stared thoughtfully at the final passage. He found himself torn between amusement and genuine respect. Lin Fang was undeniably eccentric, perhaps even perverted by normal standards—but the man had principles. He lived unapologetically by his rules and managed to ascend to a level few could even dream of.
This earned Lin Fang Leon’s admiration.

What caught Leon’s attention more than anything, however, was Lin Fang’s mention of having a Rank 5 Affinity. Leon had once assumed this was mediocre. After all, it was the same rank he had gained from the Orb of All-Elemental Affinity, identical to the affinity rank of his respected master, Seraphine. Lin Fang’s detailed explanations overturned this misconception entirely.

Contrary to Leon’s initial beliefs, even within the Ethereal Realm—a domain of prodigies—Rank 5 was still considered well above average, qualifying someone as genuinely talented. The realization brought newfound respect and optimism for Seraphine’s potential.
Yet Leon knew Seraphine’s class would inevitably limit her progress. And that’s when the autobiography introduced the shocking and terrifying concept of "Class Reawakening Dungeons."

These incredibly rare and lethal dungeons existed exclusively within the Ascendant Realm and beyond. To enter one required an unimaginable sacrifice—renouncing all previous cultivation, achievements, and even one’s existing class. The challenges within were ten times deadlier than typical Class Awakening Trials, carrying a horrific death rate of ninety-nine percent.
Survivors were never guaranteed improvements. You could end up with a class that was only slightly enhanced, completely different, or worse. Yet people risked everything on this slim chance.

Lin Fang explained in great detail why he had ventured into these dungeons. Two of his women suffered terribly poor talent—only Rank 4 affinities—barely average and doomed to shorter lifespans. Determined not to lose them prematurely, Lin Fang poured every resource at his disposal—potions, elixirs, rare artifacts, fortune-treasures—into their attempts at Class Reawakening.

Miraculously, both women survived the deadly trials and emerged triumphantly with A-ranked classes. Lin Fang candidly acknowledged they might have secured S-rank classes had it not been for their weaker Rank 4 affinities holding them back.

Reading this section profoundly impacted Leon. Lin Fang’s methods were undoubtedly questionable at times, but considering the harsh and ruthless nature of the higher realms, his actions felt justified and commendable. Lin Fang risked bankruptcy without hesitation, driven purely by loyalty and love for his companions.
Leon paused, reflecting deeply. Such devotion and self-sacrifice were rare. Lin Fang wasn’t merely a lecherous fool—he was a man capable of profound loyalty.
The autobiography further provided clear insights into affinity ranks:
- Rank 1 was lowest.
- Rank 8 was the peak.

Throughout his life, Lin Fang encountered only one individual possessing a Rank 7 affinity—the very same elf woman from the tavern incident. She belonged to the prestigious Dark Elf Clan and wielded a terrifying power even without reaching the Divine Realm. Despite being two ranks lower than Lin Fang, her aura alone made him tremble in fear. Instantly recognizing the overwhelming threat, Lin Fang didn’t attempt bravado or fight—he immediately activated his most valuable legendary-ranked escape artifact, vanishing instantly from the scene.
In his writings, Lin Fang humorously praised himself for acting quickly and avoiding the fate of foolish cultivators who underestimated opponents simply due to lower cultivation ranks.
Leon smirked knowingly at this anecdote. Lin Fang was many things, but stupid wasn’t one of them.
Lastly, Lin Fang’s book detailed a comprehensive cultivation hierarchy:
- Apprentice
- Journeyman
- Master
- Ascendant
- Sage
- Archon
- Ethereal Initiate
- Ethereal Lord
- Ethereal Sovereign
- Lesser Divinity
- Greater Divinity
- Prime Divinity
From these ranks, Leon deduced the Dark Elf Clan heir who terrified Lin Fang was likely at the Ethereal Lord stage, significantly lower than Lin Fang’s Lesser Divinity yet immensely powerful.
Moreover, Leon learned how cultivation was structured within each realm:
- Ascendant Realm housed cultivators from Apprentice to Archon.
- Ethereal Realm contained those from Apprentice to Ethereal Sovereign.
- Divine Realm ranged from Apprentice to Prime Divinity.
Lower-ranked cultivators existed within higher realms but only up to certain limits—no Archon in Earthly Realm, no Sovereign in Ascendant, and no Prime Divinity in Ethereal Realm.
This meant Leon’s current Earthly Realm’s highest attainable cultivation level was Master Rank—only Apprentice, Journeyman, and Master ranks existed here.
The gravity of this revelation settled heavily upon him. Leon realized, perhaps for the first time, how truly small and insignificant he currently was.
Yet alongside this sobering realization came excitement. He now understood the vastness and potential of his cultivation journey—one that stretched far beyond what he previously imagined.
Leon closed the book gently, determination lighting his eyes. The stairs before him stretched infinitely upward—and he was ready to climb.

chapters.title: Chapter 49: Concept and Cosmic Chat
paragraphs: There was also the mention of the level limit increased at different ranks—you had to start from Level 1 in each rank. This part wasn’t mentioned properly because most of the book consisted of sexual scenes and endeavors of Lin Fang about how he got new women.
Previously when he had checked the status screen of his master, which he didn’t know he wasn’t supposed to do, he now understood the reason behind it.

According to Lin Fang’s journey, there were three types of systems. First, the Lesser System for those below Ascendant rank. After reaching Ascendant rank, the system would get upgraded and reach the Ascendant System.
Finally, after reaching the lesser Divine rank, which meant becoming an immortal god-like existence to those below you, you would get another upgrade—a Cosmic System.

It also told about a Realm which was one rank higher than Prime Divinity. In other words, a Realm above the Divine realm. It was known only to those who had access to the Cosmic system, because of the special features like Chat and Shop, as there were entities even more powerful than them in those chats.
Prime Divinity were only ants in front of them.
Leon had some guesses, but knowing this had broadened his horizons.
But for now, he didn’t focus on this anymore and recalled the important info that he didn’t understand at first.
Concept.
It was also the same thing that had piqued his interest when he had seen it on the information tab of Seraphine.
She had a Level 1 Lightning Aura.
Concepts were divided into three stages.
Form One: Aura (4 Levels) Form Two: Embodiment (3 Levels) Form Three: Domain (3 Levels)

These concepts were the things that held back most of the people in their cultivation journey. Lin Fang mentioned the only reason he was able to become a Lesser Divinity was because he was able to Master a Domain in a secret realm which was only level 1, which enhanced his comprehension capability.
That could only be called a stroke of million-year luck.

He mentioned that even if you consumed hundreds of thousands of monster cores to reach the next ranks, you wouldn’t be able to, as these concepts were the things that separated geniuses with high comprehension ability—because of either their bloodline, special physique, or high-affinity rank—from normal folks.

Lin Fang explained how grandiose the thing concept was and how strong it could make a person. He even said that crossing the difference in level of concept in fighting was like facing a huge wall—no matter how much you tried, you couldn’t break it.
The idea of the concept fascinated Leon and it also made him see Seraphine in new light now. He had thought with his amount of mana he could defeat her, but now he wasn’t too sure about it.

Leon came out of his time dimension and stored the books inside his inventory. After that, he thanked Lin Fang in his heart as the information he had gotten from this book was priceless along with his other questionable things and techniques about pleasure.
’That was money well spent’
"I think I know more about this universe now than ever," Leon contemplated.
Now Leon opened the next section, the [Cosmic Chat]. Its name alone gave him ideas of what he should expect from it.
He was excited to see the chat between powerful entities who might be sharing secrets of the universe. He was too excited, so he opened the chat.
A message popped up in front of him.
[Please choose a name for yourself before entering the chat]
Leon thought for a while and he decided that he would use the name of his class, as he knew from before that everyone’s identities were safe in the cosmic system.
So he thought the name Elemental Paragon in his mind as a message popped up once again.
[Are you sure you want to set your username as Elemental Paragon]
[Once selected you will not be able to change your username unless you breakthrough a rank in your cultivation]
Leon didn’t see any problem in this as it felt lenient because in the future he could change his user name if he wanted.

However, he understood one thing—for normal people who got the cosmic system in the Divine Realm after entering the ranks of Lesser Divinity, it meant once they decided on their user name, they couldn’t change it for thousands of years.
That also explained why most of the people had weird nicknames when he was scrolling through the shop.
’Hmm, it might be for trying to keep their identity hidden so no trouble came their way.’

Leon didn’t think he had to worry about that as he was in a realm so below that no one could ever even guess that someone with a Cosmic system would be in there. He still didn’t understand properly why he had access to the cosmic system.
But one thing was clear—it must be due to merging with the orb of all elemental affinity.
’Yes’
After choosing yes for his username, a new message popped up.
[Welcome user Elemental Paragon into cosmic chat]
[COSMIC CHAT – THREAD #117]
Topic:The Artifact That Screams at Night
Mode:Private
Participants:@GlassToothNomad, @LibrarianOfWounds, @VelChronEmitter...
[COSMIC CHAT – THREAD #129]
Topic:How to Store a Star Without Breaking Causality
Mode:Private
Participants:@InkSleepsSoftly, @VaultNanny.exe, @TimeLoopGambler...
[COSMIC CHAT – THREAD #166]
Topic:Romantic Problems (With Eldritch Entities)
Mode:Private
Participants:@BleedsInSonatas, @HeartsEatenSoftly, @MirrorKeepsSecrets...
[COSMIC CHAT – THREAD #173]
Topic:Forbidden Cultivation Recipes (Definitely Illegal)
Mode:Private
Participants:@PanSoupOracle, @ScaldingInkChef, @WormwoodSommelier...
[COSMIC CHAT – THREAD #204]
Topic:Please Stop Resurrecting Me
Mode:Private
Participants:@DustCycleRefund, @RespawnTaxAgent, @CoffinHasWiFi...
[COSMIC CHAT – THREAD #222]
Topic:Ranking Dungeon Bosses by Dateability
Mode:Private
Participants:@LichAndLetCry, @BlushOfTheBeholder, @SwipeRightOnDOOM...
Leon looked at the different threads, but all of them were private. He couldn’t join them and see what the people were talking about inside.

He scrolled for a while trying to find if there were any chats that weren’t private. He found one—there was a search bar at the left corner too, but he had no idea what to search for, so he only scrolled.
[COSMIC CHAT – THREAD #145]
Topic:Elira’s New Concert
Mode:Public
After finding the chat, he opened it and the name of the topic was Elira’s new concert.
’Hmm, I don’t know there are things like concerts in this magical world.’
LimbDealer:
Why is every show sold out? The arena is floating in the sky.
EmberStillAlive:
Because it’s Elira. She shows up, sparkles, sings one sad song, and people lose their minds.
BoneCollector69:
I died during the second song. Not even mad.
MoonWhoEatsHerself:
You always die. Get a better body already.
MirrorJunkie:
She hit that high note and cracked all seven of my mirrors.
I’m keeping the cracks. They look nice. (。•́〈•̀。)
CausalityTaxDept:
Her voice made a group of elders younger.
They’re toddlers now. One bit me.
VortexGuy:
Okay but was she singing live?
Sounded like playback to me.
EmberStillAlive:
Don’t start that again.
Her fan club will set your realm on fire. ( ͡ಠ ʖ̯ ͡ಠ)
LimbDealer:
I still forget she’s just a Lesser Divinity.
She acts like she rules the whole divine realm.
MoonWhoEatsHerself:
That’s the brand.
She sells illusions and good lighting.
BoneCollector69:
Some guy exploded just clapping too hard.
I saw it. Very shiny way to go. ✨
MirrorJunkie:
Does she even sing?
Or just stand there glowing while everyone screams? 〵(☉⌓☉)〴
[USER DivineEcho_Elira JOINED THREAD]
DivineEcho_Elira:
"new song next week ✨ it’s calledLove me after the collapse💋"
"and no, the sparkles aren’t for sale 💅"
EmberStillAlive:
Oh stars she’s here. Be cool.
MoonWhoEatsHerself:
You cried last time she waved. (¬‿¬)
LimbDealer:
I’m not gonna lie.
I’m buying three posters this time.

chapters.title: Chapter 50: Leveling Up
paragraphs: Leon read the chat for a while, and it looked like a bunch of high schoolers talking about their favorite idol.
He couldn’t lie—he was disappointed and found it amusing how immortal beings talked like fans.

He closed the chat as he didn’t think he had anything interesting to see here, especially when most of the chats were private. Quite a few topics in the description of the chat were interesting, but he had no way to join them, so he stopped for now.

Now that he had found everything about his cosmic system and learned valuable information due to the help of the book he bought, he focused on the most important task. He had killed so many monsters inside the dungeon but hadn’t absorbed a single core. He was excited to level up and become stronger.
There were skill runes too that he had to learn.
"Let’s get started," he murmured with excitement. With just a thought, he took out a core from his inventory—the core of one of the blue electric wolves.
Holding the blue mana core in his hand, he could feel the mana radiating from it.
He started by trying to absorb mana from the core. The mana moved inside his body, and it didn’t even take a second before the stone dispersed and was absorbed by him.
Leon felt the change and a feeling of euphoria when he absorbed the core, but no message of leveling up appeared from the system.
He took out the biggest core—the red and blackish core he had gotten from the throne monster. He could feel the amount of mana inside this core was hundreds of times higher than the previous one.
Without a second thought, he started absorbing the core like before. It only took him a few seconds before his body devoured the mana core like a black hole.
While absorbing the core, not just one but three messages popped up before his eyes.
[You have reached Level 2]
[You have reached Level 3]
[You have reached Level 4]
The messages weren’t the only thing that came—he also felt that his strength had increased along with the mana reserve in his core.
He felt like he could do anything right now.
He opened the status screen with curiosity to see how much stronger he had become.
[Character Information]
[Name: Leon]
[Level: 4]
[Class: Elemental Paragon(SSS)]
[Age: 10 (Soul Age: 26)]
[Race: Human]
[Cultivation: Apprentice Rank]
[Affinity: All (Rank 7)]
[Strength: 23]
[Agility: 24]
[Stamina: 24]
[Intelligence: 130]
[Skills: None]
[Technique: Mana Body Enhancement(Adept Rank)]
First and foremost, seeing his rank 7 affinity with every element, a smile appeared on his face. He had forgotten that his passive ability was being used.
’Even in the divine realm, people with rank 7 affinity are considered geniuses. So me with rank 7 affinity with every element—how overpowered might that be considered?’
Leon couldn’t help but feel like he had hit the jackpot in the spin with that entity. Even more important was his own class, which had one passive ability to increase the rank of all his affinities.
He didn’t even feel a thing as his passive ability was active all the time, other than the fact he felt much closer to every element. His connection felt stronger than before.

He could see his strength had become 23—an increase of 15 stats, making his raw strength three times as strong as before. The same could be said for his agility and stamina; both had increased by 15 stats.
This meant five stat increases with every level up.
He remembered the strength stat of his beautiful master—it was 28 at level 10, which meant her strength increased by about 2 every rank. He understood how overpowered his class was even more now.
He was close to her stats at level 4 only.
This was especially impressive when he didn’t even think his class’s main focus was stats like strength, stamina, and agility.
He then looked at his mana, which had a massive increase of 150, meaning a 50 mana increase with every level up.
’Holy shit.’
’150 mana was more than how much total his master even had.’
And lastly, he looked at his intelligence stat, which was the lowest stat in his master’s information. This meant it might be quite hard to improve. It had also made a big jump of 30 stats.
This meant 10 stat increases with every level up.

He knew that stat was important. He had realized one thing—he felt like if he tried to cast the same spell, he would be able to do it more easily. He had a feeling about this, and also his memory had become sharp.
He still remembered every little detail from the time he had merged with the orb.

He still remembered which turn he had taken to reach the boss. He even remembered that he had killed 34 small blue wolves, 39 small red wolves, 5 big red, and 7 big blue. He even remembered which area he hit to finish them off.

His memory had reached another level. He remembered word-for-word conversations with his master. It might be presumptuous, but he felt he could plagiarize the book written by Lin Fang without even looking at it—the content was etched in his memory.
’I had become a human computer.’
He had a high desire to go to his time realm and see how strong he had become. At the same time, he wanted to practice a bit so he would be able to control his strength.

But he held off his excitement as he had more cores to absorb along with skill runes. Only then would he enter his seclusion to train his strength and try to learn concepts that his master had. Lin Fang said only one thing about it—that they were trying to learn the truth of the element.
He didn’t understand right now, but he hoped soon he would also have at least level 1 Aura like his master. Only then would he be able to call himself her equal?

If Seraphine was here to see his new strength, even now she would have been shocked to her core. His thoughts about trying to learn Level 1 Aura, which was her secret—she would have fainted in all honesty.

Leon took out all the cores at the same time, along with the boss monster core, which was around the same size as the throne monster core but with a faint color difference. He could feel the mana in this core was quite less than the previous core.

He floated all cores using his wind magic as he didn’t think he could hold them at the same time. He didn’t want to waste time absorbing one by one, and it only took him about a few seconds before they got absorbed, so he thought why not do it all at the same time.

There were more than a hundred mana cores floating in the air around him using his magic: 1 boss wolf core, 12 bigger elemental wolf cores, 73 small elemental wolf cores, and lastly 24 non-elemental small wolf cores.

With just a thought, he took out a core from his inventory—the core of one of the blue electric wolves.
Holding the blue mana core in his hand, he could feel the mana radiating from it.
He started by trying to absorb mana from the core.
The mana moved inside his body, and it didn’t even take a second before the stone dispersed and was absorbed by him.
Leon felt the change and a feeling of euphoria when he absorbed the core, but no message of leveling up appeared from the system.
He took out the biggest core—the red and blackish core he had gotten from the throne monster.
He could feel the amount of mana inside this core was hundreds of times higher than the previous one.
Without a second thought, he started absorbing the core like before.
It only took him a few seconds before his body devoured the mana core like a black hole.
While absorbing the core, not just one but three messages popped up before his eyes.
The messages weren’t the only thing that came—he also felt that his strength had increased along with the mana reserve in his core.
He felt like he could do anything right now.
He opened the status screen with curiosity to see how much stronger he had become.
First and foremost, seeing his rank 7 affinity with every element, a smile appeared on his face.
He had forgotten that his passive ability was being used.
’Even in the divine realm, people with rank 7 affinity are considered geniuses.
So me with rank 7 affinity with every element—how overpowered might that be considered?’
Leon couldn’t help but feel like he had hit the jackpot in the spin with that entity.
Even more important was his own class, which had one passive ability to increase the rank of all his affinities.
He didn’t even feel a thing as his passive ability was active all the time, other than the fact he felt much closer to every element.
His connection felt stronger than before.
He could see his strength had become 23—an increase of 15 stats, making his raw strength three times as strong as before.
The same could be said for his agility and stamina; both had increased by 15 stats.
This meant five stat increases with every level up.
He remembered the strength stat of his beautiful master—it was 28 at level 10, which meant her strength increased by about 2 every rank.
He understood how overpowered his class was even more now.
He was close to her stats at level 4 only.
This was especially impressive when he didn’t even think his class’s main focus was stats like strength, stamina, and agility.
He then looked at his mana, which had a massive increase of 150, meaning a 50 mana increase with every level up.
’150 mana was more than how much total his master even had.’
And lastly, he looked at his intelligence stat, which was the lowest stat in his master’s information.
This meant it might be quite hard to improve.
It had also made a big jump of 30 stats.
This meant 10 stat increases with every level up.
He knew that stat was important.
He had realized one thing—he felt like if he tried to cast the same spell, he would be able to do it more easily.
He had a feeling about this, and also his memory had become sharp.
He still remembered every little detail from the time he had merged with the orb.
He still remembered which turn he had taken to reach the boss.
He even remembered that he had killed 34 small blue wolves, 39 small red wolves, 5 big red, and 7 big blue.
He even remembered which area he hit to finish them off.
His memory had reached another level.
He remembered word-for-word conversations with his master.
It might be presumptuous, but he felt he could plagiarize the book written by Lin Fang without even looking at it—the content was etched in his memory.
He had a high desire to go to his time realm and see how strong he had become.
At the same time, he wanted to practice a bit so he would be able to control his strength.
But he held off his excitement as he had more cores to absorb along with skill runes.
Only then would he enter his seclusion to train his strength and try to learn concepts that his master had.
Lin Fang said only one thing about it—that they were trying to learn the truth of the element.
He didn’t understand right now, but he hoped soon he would also have at least level 1 Aura like his master.
Only then would he be able to call himself her equal?
If Seraphine was here to see his new strength, even now she would have been shocked to her core.
His thoughts about trying to learn Level 1 Aura, which was her secret—she would have fainted in all honesty.
Leon took out all the cores at the same time, along with the boss monster core, which was around the same size as the throne monster core but with a faint color difference.
He could feel the mana in this core was quite less than the previous core.
He floated all cores using his wind magic as he didn’t think he could hold them at the same time.
He didn’t want to waste time absorbing one by one, and it only took him about a few seconds before they got absorbed, so he thought why not do it all at the same time.

There were more than a hundred mana cores floating in the air around him using his magic: 1 boss wolf core, 12 bigger elemental wolf cores, 73 small elemental wolf cores, and lastly 24 non-elemental small wolf cores.
